transforms.code:
types = system.kanoa.tooling.getToolTypes({'enabled': True})
	rows = system.kanoa.utilities.convertDatasetToJSON(types) if hasattr(types, 'getRowCount') else []
	options = [{'value': r['assetTypeId'], 'label': r['assetTypeName']} for r in rows]
	# A tool made before tooling types keeps its type selectable until it's changed
	if value is not None and value not in [o['value'] for o in options]:
		current = system.kanoa.asset.getAssetTypes({'assetTypeId': value})
		if hasattr(current, 'getRowCount') and current.getRowCount():
			options.append({'value': value, 'label': '%s (not a tooling type)' % current.getValueAt(0, 'assetTypeName')})
	return options

config.script:
# A new tool starts with what its type does; an existing tool's settings stay as they are
	if self.view.custom.info.toolingAssetId is not None or self.props.value is None: return
	types = system.kanoa.tooling.getToolTypes({'assetTypeId': self.props.value})
	if not hasattr(types, 'getRowCount') or types.getRowCount() == 0: return
	for k in ('hasPositions', 'holdsInserts', 'scalesOutput', 'lifeUnit', 'calibrationIntervalDays'):
		self.view.custom.info[k] = types.getValueAt(0, k)
	return

tooltip.text: Clear this to take the tool out of service. A disabled tool can't be mounted.

The tool has pockets that hold other tools, like a mold base that holds inserts.
The machine counts this tool's cycles, not parts, so each cycle is multiplied by the parts per cycle from its positions. Shown when the tool has positions.

The unit the limits below are counted in: cycles, run minutes (time the machine is Running with the tool mounted) or calendar days.
Total life before the tool is worn out, in the life unit. Shown when Life measured in is set. Leave it empty for no limit.
Life between preventive maintenance, in the life unit. The count starts over when a PM is logged. Shown when Life measured in is set. Leave it empty for no limit.
Life between refurbishments, in the life unit. The count starts over when a refurbishment is logged. Shown when Life measured in is set. Leave it empty for no limit.
How many refurbishments the tool can have before it's worn out. It counts the refurbishments logged, so it doesn't need a life unit. Leave it empty for no limit.
How far through a limit, in percent, the tool shows as Due. Past 100% it shows as Over limit. Shown when a life unit, Max refurbishments or Calibrate every is set.
Days between calibrations. Logging a calibration moves the due date on by this many days. Leave it empty if the tool isn't calibrated.
When the next calibration is due. Logging a calibration updates it. Shown when Calibrate every is set.
